note: The worked example printed verbatim by docs.jsonata.org String Functions under $match, including the field names and the index values 0/2/5.
The documentation lists three fields for the $match object and no more; 'end' was a Go-era addition, derivable as index + $length(match), and is gone (jsntrs-eet).
'start' belongs to the matcher protocol, not to the published $match object. jsonata 2.2.2 also answers undefined here.
Non-ASCII BMP subject: index counts characters, not the UTF-8 bytes (which would be 6).

Offset UNITS pinned on an astral subject. docs.jsonata.org String Functions calls index 'the offset (starting at zero) within str of this match' without naming a unit, but the same page counts every other string position in characters -- $length 'returns the number of characters in the string str', $substring returns 'the characters in ... str starting at position start (zero-offset)'. jsntrs counts all three in Unicode code points, so index is 2 here. jsonata 2.2.2 answers 3 because it hands back the raw JS RegExp index, a UTF-16 code-unit offset -- yet its own $length('a😀b') is 3 and $substring('a😀b', 2) is 'b', so the reference is internally inconsistent and its index cannot be fed to its own $substring.
The round trip the code-point choice buys: $match's index indexes the same string $substring does.

docs.jsonata.org String Functions, $replace: 'The replacement function must take a single parameter which will be the object structure of a regex match as described in the $match function; and must return a string.' So the callback sees index. jsonata 2.2.2 passes its raw matcher object instead ({match, start, end, groups, next}), where $m.index is undefined and this expression fails D3012 -- a reference deviation from its own documented contract (jsntrs-eet).
The whole callback argument, field order included.

The matcher-protocol object, NOT the $match element: 'start'/'end' stay here, and docs.jsonata.org/regex is where they come from -- that page specifies this object field by field ('start - the starting position (zero offset) of the matching substring within the original string', 'end - the endinging position ...' [sic]). A custom matcher must return the same structure (testdata/groups/matchers/case000).
divergence: PINS A KNOWN GAP. docs.jsonata.org/regex also specifies 'next - when invoked, will return details of the second occurrence of any matching substring (and so on)', and jsntrs does not build it (jsonata 2.2.2 does). This case asserts whole-object equality against a four-key object, so it pins the ABSENCE of a documented field. Kept as a regression pin of current behaviour, not as a claim that four keys are correct. Tracked as jsntrs-h77; when 'next' is built this case must be re-derived -- probably by asserting individual fields, since the harness rejects any object holding a function value (crates/jsntrs/tests/conformance.rs:479-481) and requires equal key counts (:510-513).

note: A user matcher reports 'start'; $match republishes it as 'index'. The subject is astral so the translation is visibly character-based on both sides ($length inside the matcher and index out of it agree).
